compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
When the store wedges (dirty tracker tree, stale locks, stranded merge state), today's tooling is partial: `rebar fsck` checks event integrity but does not report the dirty-tree class that caused the recent P0 wedges (tracked working-tree deletions of store artifacts, untracked regenerable compaction leftovers, orphaned lock files, orphaned `.tmp-event-*`); `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` handles only a stranded index and foreign worktree paths (verified: its `_stranded_paths`/`_foreign_worktree_paths` scans reported 0 findings while the store sat wedged with 119 tracked `.archived` deletions); the documented recovery for the live wedges was ad-hoc raw git under the write lock, recorded by hand on tickets 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa / e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73. Operators (and agents) need one sanctioned, non-destructive door: fsck DETECTS the class, doctor --repair HEALS it.

## Approach
Detection: add a tracker-dirty check to the fsck surface (src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py, which already owns tracker-level health lines) that classifies `git status --porcelain` output into: (1) tracked deletions of store artifacts restorable from HEAD, (2) untracked regenerable compaction leftovers (`*-SNAPSHOT.json`, `*.retired` whose retired-source is already folded), (3) orphaned `.tmp-event-*` (never auto-touched — named for manual triage), plus lock-artifact staleness reported via the existing doctor_locks scan. Each class gets a distinct finding line, and the JSON contract is wired end-to-end: fsck's JSON is produced by `_transform_json` in src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py over a fixed `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` set, so the three new tracker-dirty kinds are registered there (each emitting a `KIND: detail` line whose detail carries count + paths) — fsck.py is an explicit edit target, not an implied one.
Repair: extend `rebar doctor --repair` (src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py's existing scan/repair_finding registry pattern) with repair actions using TWO lock windows, because the store write lock (rebar._store.lock.write_lock) is non-reentrant — doctor's own `run_repair` deliberately holds NO outer lock (its regression test pins that an outer hold starves inner per-write acquisitions), and `sync.reconverge` acquires the write lock internally. So: (window 1) the raw file-mutating steps — restore class-1 paths via `git checkout --` (non-destructive; bytes exist at HEAD) and move class-2 paths into the quarantine directory established by change 1757 (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/` — move, never delete) — run under one short-lived scoped write_lock acquisition, through the store seam (gitutil.run_git), and that lock is RELEASED before convergence; (window 2) the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) is then invoked and takes the write lock itself, converging the previously wedged store in the same command. Class-3 paths are left untouched and printed. Safety envelope: before the first mutating repair, record a backup ref (`refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts>` pointing at the tickets HEAD) mirroring the backup-ref + durable-audit envelope `tracker-maintenance` actually provides (tracker-maintenance holds no write lock; its envelope is the backup ref plus audited raw `_git` calls — that, not a lock, is the precedent adopted here), and every action is recorded in the doctor output. Positive rationale: doctor already owns scan-classify-repair with typed findings; extending its registry avoids inventing a second repair CLI.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py — tracker-dirty classification (text lines).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — register the three tracker-dirty kinds in `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` / extend `_transform_json` so fsck --output json carries per-class counts and paths.
- src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py — new finding types + repair actions (scoped write_lock window for file mutations; backup ref; post-release reconverge call).
- tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py (new) — seeded-wedge end-to-end coverage.
- docs/user-guide.md — document the new fsck findings and doctor repairs.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture tracker seeded with all three classes plus a diverged origin; `rebar fsck` names each class; `rebar doctor --repair` restores class 1, quarantines class 2 (bytes preserved), leaves class 3 in place, and the store converges (ahead/behind 0/0, `git status` clean except class 3).
- Failure/edge: doctor --repair on a CLEAN store makes zero changes and zero commits (idempotent); the file-mutating window respects existing lock semantics (a held write lock makes it wait/fail per the lock contract rather than mutate unlocked); class-3 files are byte-identical after the run; the backup ref exists after a mutating repair and is absent after a no-op run.
- Lock discipline: a test asserts the write lock is NOT held when reconverge is entered (mirroring doctor's existing test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_event_writes pattern), and IS held during the checkout/move steps.
- JSON contract: fsck --output json carries the per-class counts and paths (via the registered kinds).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar fsck` on a seeded dirty tracker reports each class with a distinct finding id in text AND in `--output json` (counts + paths); clean stores report none; checked by the new test.
- [ ] `rebar doctor --repair` heals a seeded wedge end-to-end (tree clean apart from `.tmp-event-*`, merge converged, no event bytes lost — quarantine holds moved files, backup ref recorded); checked by the end-to-end test.
- [ ] Each file-mutating repair step runs under its own scoped write-lock acquisition, the lock is released before reconverge (which self-locks), and no repair path deletes a file (moves or restores only); checked by lock-state assertions and quarantine contents in the test.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
